ledger.claim: The reroute the rider complains of is on the platform's own record. The vehicle left the recommended route at the TPE / Tampines Avenue 7 exit at 08:40:24 and rejoined it at Simei Avenue / Changi Business Park Avenue 1 at 08:48:22, running Tampines Avenue 7 and Simei Avenue — the roads the rider names — and the GPS trace shows that same route fix by fix across those eight minutes. POL-RD-22 uses the trace for exactly this purpose: showing which route was taken and when. This is not a disputed detour; it is a recorded one.

The deviation is not traffic-justified. The LTA advisory retrieved for the very segment the driver blames — Tampines Expressway towards PIE at Tampines Avenue 7, valid 07:59:37 to 09:29:37, which overlaps the trip window of 08:29:37 to 08:49:37 — records advisory type NONE: no incident, no roadwork, no closure, and speed bands 4-5 throughout, with justifies_reroute false. POL-RD-23 provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, so the driver's counter-statement ('the TPE exit to PIE got queue in the morning') carries no weight against the official data.

The driver gave the rider no notice of the deviation, before it or at the point of it, and the rider never agreed to it. POL-RD-21 permits a reroute only in response to real-time traffic, a closure or congestion, and only where the driver informs the rider by in-app chat or by a verbal notice evidenced by a call recording. Neither condition is met: this trip's chat log is complete and carries zero messages, the trip record carries no in-app calls, messages_during_trip is empty, and no call recording exists in the record at all. No notice and no agreement is established, so this is not an agreed deviation.

I do not press the rider's 5.00 SGD or his 4 km estimate, because the record does not carry them and I will not stretch it. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation on the platform's recorded distances, and 12.8 km actual less 12.0 km recommended is 0.80 km — inside the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 and the route-deviation thresholds set. The rider was charged 19.64 SGD with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so he carries the charge; but the rider's complaint is about the manner of this reroute — unjustified and unannounced — not about a distance the policy treats as tolerable, and the money claim is not made out beyond what the matrix provides.

The rider's suspicion that the driver 'does it to everyone' cannot ground a finding on this trip. POL-GEN-01 confines profile use to rider_profile.fraud_flags and driver_profile.fraud_flags, and only for POL-GEN-22's confidence uplift, and to rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d under POL-NS-25; neither profile here carries a fraud flag, and every other profile field — the driver's prior deviation flags, the rider's claim history — is context only. No profile fact raises the confidence bar, and this case turns on this trip's own record.

The deviation on this trip is 0.80 km, and that is the only figure the policy allows anyone to use. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation distance is the platform's recorded distances — trip_record.actual_distance_km (12.8 km) minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km (12.0 km) — and the GPS trace is expressly not used to re-measure distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. Trip record and trace are both COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The rider's '4 km out of the way' and his Google Maps comparison are estimates, not the recorded distances POL-RD-22 makes the measure, and they are contradicted by the platform's own telemetry.

POL-RD-22 makes a deviation of 1.0 km or less within tolerance, and 0.80 km is within it. POL-RD-24 says exactly one row of its matrix applies, and both rows that can apply to a within-tolerance deviation — row (c) (traffic-justified, rider not informed) and row (e) (not traffic-justified) — return no refund. There is no row of the POL-RD-24 matrix that pays anything where the deviation is 1 km or less, so the rider cannot recover whatever the traffic question is answered.

The very most any route-deviation refund could be on these figures is the excess distance fare — deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd — which is 0.80 x 0.72 = 0.58 SGD, without surge, per the POL-RD-24 formula. That is the ceiling on the rider's claim, not the 5.00 SGD he asks, and because the deviation is within the 1.0 km tolerance even that 0.58 SGD is not payable.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03 and never means 'restore a charge'. The rider filed this dispute, and the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0 — the present state is that the metered fare of 19.64 SGD stands and nothing has been returned. A ruling that the rider's claim is not supported therefore leaves the charge exactly where it is and leaves the driver with his fare.

The traffic advisory does not give the rider a route to a refund either. Its type is NONE and it records no incident, roadwork or closure, so POL-RD-23 is not satisfied and the reroute is not traffic-justified — which places this case in the not-traffic-justified limb of POL-RD-24, row (e), where a deviation of 1 km or less still yields no refund. The advisory is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and it plainly overlaps the trip window; it just does not change the tolerance outcome.

I do not contest that the chat log holds no messages and no in-app call is recorded, so notice of the deviation under POL-RD-21 is not established on this record. That fact is immaterial to the money: POL-RD-24 pays an excess-distance refund only where the deviation exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, and this deviation is 0.80 km. The chat log is a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0; its emptiness costs the driver nothing here.

Nothing on this record requires escalation. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, at which the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and neither profile carries a fraud_flags value of 1 or more, so the 0.95 confidence band is not engaged. POL-RD-25's own condition is met on this record, and the deviation is 0.80 km so its held-back 2 km limb (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) has no purchase. This dispute can and should be decided now.

The rider's insinuation that 'this driver has had complaints like this before' and 'does it to everyone' is unsupported by any artifact in this case, and it cannot decide anything even if true. POL-GEN-01 confines the use of party history to two named fields — fraud_flags and no_show_cancellations_30d — and every other profile field is context only and may never establish a fact about THIS trip or decide its outcome. The only artifacts touching a party's history are the profile snapshots, and they are barred from grounding a finding on the rider's pattern allegation.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you largely agree on the facts, and the record bears that out. The platform's recorded distances are 12.8 km actual against 12.0 km recommended — a deviation of 0.80 km (POL-RD-22; trip record EV-TRIP-05018). POL-RD-22 measures the deviation on those recorded distances and expressly does not re-measure from the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05018), whose 10.789 km reading understates a sparse route. A deviation of 1.0 km or less is within tolerance, and 0.80 km is inside it, so the rider's '4 km out of the way' and Google Maps comparison are estimates rather than the measure the policy uses and are contradicted by the platform's own telemetry.

The reroute did happen: the vehicle left the recommended route at the TPE / Tampines Avenue 7 exit at 08:40:24 and rejoined at Simei Avenue / Changi Business Park Avenue 1 at 08:48:22 (route events in EV-TRIP-05018, matched fix-by-fix by the trace). The LTA advisory for that very segment — Tampines Expressway towards PIE, valid 07:59:37–09:29:37, overlapping the trip window — records type NONE: no incident, roadwork or closure, and speed bands 4–5, so under POL-RD-23 the reroute is not traffic-justified and the driver's account of a morning queue does not establish otherwise. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05018) is complete with zero messages and the trip record carries no in-app calls, so no notice or agreement is established under POL-RD-21.

Applying the POL-RD-24 matrix, exactly one row applies. The deviation is 1 km or less and the reroute is not traffic-justified, so row (e) governs: no refund, within tolerance. The most the excess-distance formula could ever produce is 0.80 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.58 SGD, and the tolerance means even that is not payable. The rider filed this dispute and is owed nothing, so the outcome is NO_ACTION: both amounts are null and the present state stands — the metered fare of 19.64 SGD remains charged, with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 (EV-FARE-05018).

No profile history was used to decide this trip (POL-GEN-01): the rider's suggestion that the driver 'does it to everyone' has nothing behind it, and the profile snapshots cannot ground a finding either way. On value, 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the AI may decide; confidence 0.90 meets POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar, and POL-RD-25's held-back 2 km limb (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) is not engaged at 0.80 km. No route-deviation clause produces a referral, so none is listed.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
